liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **West L.A. Fadeaway** (2 reviews): Characterized as mournful, featuring a notable ginger verse; Noted for funky lyrics near the end that make listeners sit up [20][25]
- **Loser** (2 reviews): Described as melancholy, part of a set full of the band's saddest songs; Described as a killer performance following the West L.A. Fadeaway [20][26]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Described as insane and one of the better performances heard recently [25]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Identified as a soulful performance within the emotional set [20]
- Highlighted as the opening song for the New York City show [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-09-21.mtx.seamons.97705.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4.6/5 by 15 [1]
- **gd1982-09-21.sbd.miller.33684.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 167 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1982-09-21.sbd.miller.109209.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 170 min; rated 4.57/5 by 7 [5]
- **gd1982-09-21.163450.senn441.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 177 min [7]
- **gd1982-09-21.119147.nak300.chasingwilma.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 169 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [12]

## Around the show

- Attendee notes the Garden venue provided significant energy despite security hassles [21]
- Reviewer claims the entire tour from the South to Portland had no weak nights [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-09-21.mtx.seamons.97705.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [1]. Also: Lineage includes Senn 421s to cassette, then DAT, CD, and FLAC by Charlie Miller; Jim Wise recorded from 18th row center using Sennheiser 421s and Sony TC-D5 [1]
- **gd1982-09-21.sbd.miller.33684.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat [3]. Also: DAT to CD transfer completed in October 1999, though lineage confirmation is uncertain [3]
- **gd1982-09-21.sbd.miller.109209.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat [5]. Also: Job B. Jones assisted with the pitch correction for the recording [5]
- **gd1982-09-21.163450.senn441.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob, Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Nakamichi 550 (21st row, DFC) [7]. Also: Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 source supplies a 5:26 patch in the Drums section [7]
- **gd1982-09-21.119147.nak300.chasingwilma.flac16**: taped by chasingwilma; transferred by chasingwilma; source: nak 300 (fob)> d-5sony> mc [12]. Also: Recording identified as an FOB made by Jim Wise using Sennheiser 421 microphones [27]
